Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

suitable adjective

also appropriate (for a purpose), suited, fit for, right for, unsuitable, good for (a purpose)

classical

Caes. B.G. 2.8.3: locō … opportūnō atque idōneō (Lewis & Short)
Cic. Lael. 62: ad amīcitiam esse idōneus

idōneus, idōnea, idōneum

adjective; with ad + gerund, the dative, or quī + subjunctive · Declension on Wiktionary

fit, suitable (for a purpose)

The everyday word, of things and of people (a person fit or capable for a task).

Other words

  • aptus, apta, aptum — suited, fitted to

    adjective; with ad or the dative, of persons always the dative · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.231: calceī habilēs et aptī ad pedem (Lewis & Short, s.v. apō); Liv. 1.45: apta diēs sacrificiō · Declension on Wiktionary

    Literally fastened, joined (the participle of an old verb apere); so fitted to something, suitable. It can also mean ready, equipped.

  • accommodātus, accommodāta, accommodātum — adapted to, appropriate to

    adjective; with ad or the dative · also used · classical · Caes. B.G. 3.13: puppēs ad magnitūdinem flūctuum accommodātae (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    A prose word (Lewis & Short), of things made or chosen to fit a purpose.

Examples

  • apēs, ut ajunt, dēbēmus imitārī, quae vagantur et flōrēs ad mel faciendum idōneōs carpunt

    we should copy the bees, as they say, which wander and pick the flowers fit for making honeySen. Ep. 84.3

  • calceī habilēs et aptī ad pedem

    shoes that are easy to wear and fit the footCic. de Or. 1.231 (Lewis & Short)

  • Haec vestis ad nūptiās nōn est idōnea.

    These clothes aren’t suitable for a wedding.composed

See also appropriate, fit, useful, able.
